subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes and unit economics

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes and unit economics

Thanks again for taking time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Primary goals: lower latency for customer chat experiences and improve semantic search relevance for product docs.
- Model mix we discussed (initial): chat (customer chat/in-app assistants), embeddings (search/semantic rank), occasional rerank for top-N results.
- Immediate ask: to scope pricing I need rough monthly token volumes by model class and a target budget range (monthly or $/1M tokens target if you prefer unit economics).

Can you confirm ballpark monthly volumes across:
  • Chat (avg prompt+response 750 tokens / convo)
  • Embeddings (avg doc chunk 1500 tokens)
  • Rerank (per-request token multiply)

Example helpful response: total tokens/month and % split across chat/embeddings/rerank, and any seasonality. Also flag if procurement or legal should be looped in now (cc’ing Rafael on this thread for SE/implementation questions).

Tentative next steps: I’ll send a short pricing estimate (per-model unit economics + example monthly bill) once we have volumes, then we can decide if you want a formal quote.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes and unit economics

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below (roughs for now; will push Sam for a more formal forecast):

- Estimated total tokens / month (starting baseline): ~120M tokens
  • Chat: 60% (~72M tokens) — majority is user prompts + generated responses (avg ~750 tokens/convo)
  • Embeddings: 30% (~36M tokens) — nightly indexing of product docs and user queries (avg chunk ~1500 tokens)
  • Rerank: 10% (~12M tokens) — used for search result reordering (avg per-request overhead ~50 tokens)

- Budget guidance: initial procurement target is $10k–$25k/month for experimentation phase. If unit economics work, would expand to $40k+/month.

Procurement (procurement@acme.com) is looped for visibility — they’ll request a formal quote and T&C before we proceed. Sam (cc’d) is working on a finer token forecast and will share the spreadsheet.

Let me know any quick assumptions you used so I can sanity-check with finance.

— Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes and unit economics

Great — thanks Alex, that’s super helpful. I pulled together a quick estimate and a couple of unit economics examples so you can see the impact by model class. Attached: redwood_pricing_estimate_ACME_Q2.pdf and the forecast template you can fill in (acme_token_forecast.xlsx).

High-level assumptions I used:
- Chat model: gpt-chat-v2 (approx) — $15 / 1M tokens (example blended rate for service + infra; exact varies by model variant and quantization).
- Embeddings: embed-lite-v1 — $6 / 1M tokens.
- Rerank (light rerank model): $3 / 1M tokens (per-token cost for short inference).

Example baseline math (using your split, 120M tokens/month):
- Chat: 72M tokens => 72 * $15 = $1,080
- Embeddings: 36M => 36 * $6 = $216
- Rerank: 12M => 12 * $3 = $36
- Total estimated spend ≈ $1,332 / month on model inference

Notes and caveats:
- The numbers above are illustrative — typical enterprise deals include volume discounts, committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) options, and potential batching/kv-cache reductions that lower effective $/1M tokens.
- For a $10k–$25k/month target you’re well above the illustrative baseline; it suggests either your real volumes are higher than the rough 120M or you expect to include higher-cost model variants (e.g., specialized instruction-tuned or longer-context chat models).

If it’s helpful, Rafael (SE) can run a quick sensitivity with different model variants (e.g., cheaper quantized chat vs. high-accuracy chat) and show the tradeoff between cost and latency/quality. Rafael — can you do a 1-pager with 3 scenarios (conservative/expected/expanded) and attach expected latency ranges?

Next steps:
1) Sam / procurement to share the more detailed token forecast (Sam — any chance to send the sheet this week?)
2) I’ll convert this into a formal quote and a 3-scenario pricing summary once we have the detailed volumes.
3) If procurement needs an NDA/PO or additional security evidence, let me know — we can surface SOC2 / data handling docs quickly.

Thanks — Marissa
